thread.title: Lessons Investors Can Learn From the Tesla, Elon Musk Drama

title: Lessons Investors Can Learn From the Tesla, Elon Musk Drama

organizations.name: elon musk drama lessons investors can learn from

text: Lessons Investors Can Learn From the Tesla, Elon Musk Drama By aapl During the past week Tesla ( TSLA ) has traded in a 42-point range. The volatility was triggered by Elon Musk's tweets that he was considering the idea of taking Tesla private at a price of $420 and that he had already secured the necessary financing. The manner in which this announcement was made was so unusual that many people thought that Musk's Twitter ( TWTR ) account had been hacked. The stock was halted before it was eventually confirmed that it really was Mr. Musk communicating this news via Twitter. The SEC was reportedly investigating the way this was done and the stock sunk below the price that it was at when the Musk tweet was made. Many market participants questioned whether it would even be possible to finance such a deal. The stock popped back up late on Thursday following news that Tesla would hold a board meeting to consider Musk's "going private" proposal. Tesla shares rose less than 1% on Friday, finishing the week at $355.49.The story will continue next week. It is an interesting corporate drama but what lessons can investors learn from this? The most important lesson is that there is a small group of stocks that are battlegrounds. They have a dedicated group of supporters that believe that the stock is one of the greatest investments ever. They also have a group of critics that believe the stock is widely overhyped and will ultimately go bust. Emotions on both sides run extremely high and this 'boom or bust' battle leads to unusually high volatility. Both sides think the other side is wildly deluded. Other stocks in the past such as Amazon ( AMZN ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) have been major battlegrounds. Over time they have greatly rewarded those that believed in the story and were able to withstand the intense battles. However, there have been other battleground stocks like Enron, WorldCom and Tyco that turned out to be the massive frauds that the critics thought they were. Battleground stocks often have charismatic leadership that attracts followers that are looking for the next Steve Jobs of Apple ( AAPL ) or Jeff Bezos of Amazon. Their unique management style appeals to a great many but it also attracts the skeptics that believe the bombast and unorthodox style is just covering up some significant flaws. What is important for investors is to recognize that a stock is a battleground. Tesla is either going to be one of the great business stories of the century or one of the biggest flops. There is unlikely to be a middle ground. This is a stock that will either soar or crash and burn. If you are believer in the Tesla story the most important thing you can do is to find a way to control your risk should your belief turn out to be incorrect. There must be a point where you draw the line and admit that your forecast for the future of Tesla is incorrect, but setting that parameter is one of the most difficult things to do in investing. Investors often fail to understand that it isn't the accuracy of their predictions that is the most important thing but their plans for dealing with inaccurate predictions that will determine their level of success. You must prevent the mistakes from taking too much of your capital. If you hold a strong belief about the ultimate outcome of Tesla then you better have a strong appetite for volatility. During the past year the stock has moved in a range from as high as $387 down to $244 and back up again. Virtually any reasonable money management approach would have shaken out both bulls and bears with that degree of movement. You must have some very strong convictions if you are willing to let a stock drop more than 35% without shaking you out. If you using a money management system that cuts your losses at some point then keep in mind that you can always buy the stock back. Just because a stop was triggered doesn't mean you have so stay on the sidelines. Think of a stop loss as just a form of temporary insurance rather than a significant event that freezes you form any further action. The lesson for investors is that battleground stocks like Tesla require an unusual amount of patience as well as a very high tolerance for volatility. The folks that stay with this stock have to be rabid in their beliefs. They must be true believers that think Musk is a genius that will totally transform the auto industry. If you don't have that conviction, then owning this stock will likely be a painful experience as you watch the drama continue for years to come.
